test_title: PYST 29: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: When a gun is fired, why does the gun experience a recoil even though the bullet moves forward?

options.text: Because the bullet’s acceleration is less than the gun’s
Because the bullet exerts an equal and opposite force on the gun
Because the gun’s mass is smaller than the bullet’s
Because the gun pushes the bullet forward with less force

solution:
The correct answer is __**Because the bullet exerts an equal and opposite force on the gun**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phenomenon of a gun moving backward when a bullet is fired is known as **recoil**. This is a direct application of **Newton’s Third Law of Motion**, which states that for every **action**, there is an **equal and opposite reaction**.
 
• When the **gunpowder** in a cartridge explodes, it creates **expanding gases** that exert a huge **force** on the **bullet**, pushing it forward through the barrel. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Simultaneously, according to the **law of action and reaction**, the **bullet** exerts an exactly **equal amount of force** back onto the **gun** in the **opposite direction**.
 
• The **forward motion** of the bullet is the **action**, and the **backward motion** of the gun is the **reaction**.
 
• While the **forces** acting on the gun and the bullet are **equal in magnitude**, their resulting **accelerations** differ significantly because of the vast difference in their **masses**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Law of Conservation of Momentum:**

 
 
• The **recoil of a gun** can also be explained using the **Law of Conservation of Momentum**. This law states that the **total momentum** of an isolated system remains **constant** if no external force acts on it.
 
• Before firing, the **initial momentum** of both the **gun** and the **bullet** is **zero** because they are at **rest**.
 
• After firing, the **final momentum** must also be **zero**. Therefore, the **positive momentum** of the bullet (moving forward) must be balanced by the **negative momentum** of the gun (moving backward).
 
• Mathematically: **m × v + M × V = 0**, where **m** and **v** are the mass and velocity of the bullet, and **M** and **V** are the mass and velocity of the gun.
 
 
 
• **Recoil Velocity:**
 
 
• The **recoil velocity (V)** of the gun is given by **V = -(m × v) / M**.
 
• Because the **mass of the gun (M)** is much **larger** than the **mass of the bullet (m)**, the **recoil velocity** is much **smaller** than the **bullet's velocity**.
 
• This explains why the gun moves back with a **jerk** rather than flying back at the same speed as the bullet.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Second Law in Context:**
 
 
• According to **Newton's Second Law (F = ma)**, for a **constant force**, **acceleration** is **inversely proportional** to **mass**.
 
• The **bullet**, having a **very small mass**, experiences a **tremendous acceleration**. The **gun**, having a **large mass**, experiences a **small acceleration**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Analysis of Incorrect Options:**

 
 
• **Option 1:** The bullet's **acceleration** is actually much **greater** than the gun’s, not less, due to its **smaller mass**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Option 3:** In reality, a **gun's mass** is always **larger** than the **bullet's mass** to minimize the **recoil velocity** and ensure the safety of the user. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Option 4:** According to **Newton’s Third Law**, the **force** pushed by the gun on the bullet and the force pushed by the bullet on the gun are **exactly equal** in magnitude. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:**
 
 
• Soldiers are trained to hold a gun **tightly against their shoulder**. This effectively **increases the mass (M)** by adding the **shooter's body mass** to the gun's mass, thereby **reducing the recoil velocity** and preventing injury.
 
• **Muzzle brakes** or **recoil pads** are often used in modern firearms to **absorb** or **redirect** some of the **kinetic energy** generated during the **recoil**.
